text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes often develops slowly over years, and many people have no obvious symptoms in the early stages.

list.snippet: Frequent urination: Needing to go to the bathroom more often, especially at night, as your kidneys try to flush out extra sugar.
Excessive thirst: Feeling constantly thirsty because frequent urination leads to mild dehydration.
Persistent fatigue: Feeling unusually tired or drained because your cells cannot effectively absorb glucose for energy.
Blurred vision: High blood sugar causing fluid shifts that swell the lenses of your eyes.
Slow-healing wounds: Minor cuts, bruises, or sores taking a long time to heal due to poor circulation and immune function.
Tingling or numbness: A "pins and needles" sensation, burning, or pain in the hands or feet from early nerve irritation (neuropathy).
Unexplained weight changes: Losing weight without trying because the body cannot absorb glucose properly, or sometimes gaining weight linked to insulin resistance.
Increased hunger: Feeling hungry (polyphagia) even after eating because energy isn't reaching your cells.
Darkened skin patches: Developing velvety, dark patches of skin (acanthosis nigricans) around the neck, armpits, or groin, which indicate insulin resistance.
Frequent infections: Experiencing repeat urinary tract infections (UTIs), yeast infections, or skin issues because bacteria and fungi thrive on high sugar levels.

text_blocks.snippet: Because symptoms can be subtle or absent, doctors diagnose Type 2 diabetes using simple blood tests:

list.snippet: A1C test: Measures average blood sugar over the past 2 to 3 months (6.5% or higher indicates diabetes).
Fasting plasma glucose test: Measures blood sugar after an 8-hour fast (126 mg/dL or higher indicates diabetes).
Random plasma glucose test: Checked at any time without fasting (200 mg/dL or higher indicates diabetes).

text_blocks.snippet: You can read more about diagnostic criteria and management through the Cleveland Clinic Type 2 Diabetes Guide or review comprehensive symptom breakdowns from the Mayo Clinic Type 2 Diabetes Overview.
